newsitem.title: POLAND: RECENT ZLOTY RISE NOT ON FOREIGN INFLOWS- C.BANK.
newsitem.headline: RECENT ZLOTY RISE NOT ON FOREIGN INFLOWS- C.BANK.

text.p: The rise of the Polish zloty to four percent from the centre of the trading band, which triggered central bank interventions, was not fuelled by foreign inflows, deputy central bank president said on Tuesday.

Witold Kozinski told a news conference that had fresh foreign funds been flowing into the system, banks repeatedly hit by intervention purchases would not need to buy currencies back from the National Bank of Poland.

"On January 20 we intervened for the first time...taking the zloty down to three percent from about 4.1 percent by buying $90 million, but at the post trade fixing banks come to the NBP to buy back as much as $60 million," Kozinski said.
"It was a clear signal that the strengthening of the zloty was not, in any way, connected to higher supply of currencies on the forex," he added.
The NBP intervened against the zloty again on Wednesday and Friday and in all three instances, Kozinski said, banks sustained losses.

"The bottom line is that the zloty's rise was created... mostly by unidentified factors...to a small extent because of the dollar/mark cross...and in the least by a supply of foreign currencies," he said.

Last week dealers said the zloty's bullish mood was fuelled mostly by foreign inevstors taking Polish positions at the start of the year, attracted by high real interest rates and expectations of a cut in the zloty's monthly devaluation rate.
They also noted Poland's plans to meet European Monetary Union's requirements for joining in 2004 and better than expected 1996 fundamentals.
